g.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Dot: estimate at the main XGBoost tuning setting. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Dashed rules: no difference, and the 1 point improvement that the positive control must exceed. Each row is the control's error minus the error of the arm it pads, scored on the same hours. The report's leaderboard gives each arm's own error. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar. F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective energy (CAPE), convective inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface temperature, snow, precipitation, pressure, wind, gusts. IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day. Negative control: the arm's columns, with the new variables replaced by copies shuffled among the hours that share a farm, a month, and an hour of day, so only each month's mean at each hour survives. Controls named F2 + shuffled direct radiation, F4 variables, or F5 variables pad F2 with only that group's shuffled variables. Positive control: F2 plus CAMS's satellite-derived irradiance, a column that must help. Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, March 2024 to April 2026. IFS: ECMWF's forecast via Open-Meteo. CAMS:
satellite irradiance service.
Dot: estimate at the main XGBoost tuning setting. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Dashed rules: no
difference, and the 1 point improvement that the positive control must exceed.
Each row is the control's error minus the error of the arm it pads, scored on the same hours. The report's
leaderboard gives each arm's own error.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given, beside sun position and calendar.
F0: IFS radiation and air temperature. Each set adds to the one before. F1: total cloud cover. F2: low, mid, and
high cloud cover. F3: direct radiation. F4: dew point, column water vapour, boundary-layer height. F5: convective
energy (CAPE), convective inhibition, visibility. F6 (all 20 IFS variables): surface temperature, snow,
precipitation, pressure, wind, gusts.
IFS: ECMWF's 9 km forecast, 00 UTC run, read at a lead day.
Negative control: the arm's columns, with the new variables replaced by copies shuffled among the hours that share
a farm, a month, and an hour of day, so only each month's mean at each hour survives.
Controls named F2 + shuffled direct radiation, F4 variables, or F5 variables pad F2 with only that group's shuffled
variables.
Positive control: F2 plus CAMS's satellite-derived irradiance, a column that must help.
Lead day L: the forecast was issued L days before the day it describes, so lead day 1 is the morning before.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
